title: Can hand-drawn strokes keep a diagram’s layout?
answer: Lay the chart out first and let the hand only trace it, so a new drawing changes each stroke’s wobble and leaves every box where the layout put it

checks.question: Give the spring hand of the third step the opening’s route instead: a point that moves corner to corner as the opening’s hand did, each line starting where the last one stopped and up to 2° and 3% off. Would words still poke out of their boxes?
checks.answer: Yes. The spring keeps the ink close to whatever route it chases, but that route has wandered just as the opening’s boxes did, so the boxes still end up far from where the layout put them. The opening’s drawing was made exactly this way. What keeps the words inside is a route laid out before any ink; the spring only keeps each stroke near its route.

checks.question: Lower the spring hand’s damping to a quarter of its value, so the pen overshoots at every corner before settling. Would a second drawing then move any box?
checks.answer: No. The ink would stray further from its marks, about 0.02 units instead of 0.005 in this model. But each stroke still starts at rest on its own laid-out mark and chases only that mark, so the overshoot never carries into the next stroke, and every box stays where the layout put it.

steps.title: Can a wobbling hand draw this timeline and keep its words in their boxes?
steps.line: What must be fixed before any ink?
steps.caption: The words stayed where the layout placed them, but 2 of 8 poke out of their boxes. This simulated hand chained imperfect moves, every line setting off from where the previous one stopped. A displaced endpoint became the next line’s starting point. What must be fixed before the ink begins?
steps.picture: Code, 5 lines; The timeline’s four lines of text, and below them the timeline drawn by a hand that sets off each line from where the last stopped: its boxes, rings and strings wander from left to right, and 2 of the 8 words, outlined in red, stick out of their boxes.

steps.title: If the hand places the boxes, a second drawing moves them
steps.line: Grey: the first drawing. Dark: the second. Dashed: where the boxes belong.
steps.caption: Each imperfect move changes where the next one begins, so every error is carried into every later corner. Across four boxes the small deviations accumulate: two seeds place the same box as much as 0.52 units apart. Could the pen wobble without deciding the next box’s position?
steps.picture: Dusk. Midnight. Small hours. Dawn. Up to 0.52 units apart: the boxes moved.

steps.title: With the route fixed first, two drawings stay on it
steps.line: Blue band: the route the layout fixed. Grey and dark: two drawings of it.
steps.caption: The route now fixes the corners before drawing. A simulated pen follows it like a mass pulled by a damped spring, and the next stroke starts from its own fixed mark. The magnifier shows different ink near the same route. The fix, in this hand model: lay the chart out first and let the hand only trace it, so a new drawing changes each stroke’s wobble and leaves every box where the layout put it.
steps.picture: Blue: the route the layout fixed. ×36: 0.003 apart. Two drawings, within 0.005 units of it.

steps.title: For the real timeline, Agentic Mermaid fixes every box first
steps.line: Every box, marker and label has its place before any ink.
steps.caption: Agentic Mermaid turns the timeline text into geometry: it places every period box, marker and event box, sizing the boxes using Inter’s letter widths. The hand receives those positions rather than deciding them while it draws. rough.js uses the same separation in its rectangle API: the caller supplies the corner and size, while roughness affects the strokes.
steps.picture: Timeline: 4 periods; Code, 5 lines; A dimension line marked “2.96 units”. Measured: Midnight Wick trimmed.

steps.title: The hand is given the layout’s marks and nothing else
steps.line: Blue pencil: the route the chart’s ink follows.
steps.caption: Agentic Mermaid lays the real timeline out first, sizing each box from its words’ measured widths. The construction pencil traces those fixed outlines, and the ink then follows them. These marks separate where the chart belongs from how its strokes look; they are the same in both drawings. The 8 words have places to fit before either drawing begins.
steps.picture: Code, 5 lines; The timeline’s layout traced in thin blue construction pencil: 4 period boxes, 4 event boxes, their markers and strings, the rail and an empty box where each word will go; 1 label. New in this step: The timeline’s layout traced in thin blue construction pencil: 4 period boxes, 4 event boxes, their markers and strings, the rail and an empty box where each word will go; 1 label.

steps.title: Close on Midnight’s marker, the ink lies on the blue ring
steps.line: Pale blue band: the ring as laid out. Dark line: the spring hand’s ink.
steps.caption: The pale band is the fixed ring; the dark line is the spring hand’s ink. This ring strays at most 0.002 units from its route, while the largest deviation across the chart is 0.005. A wobbly stroke can remain close to its route without making the next object inherit its error.

New in this step: Midnight’s marker in blue construction pencil: its ring as a pale band, the dot inside and the string below; Close on the Midnight marker: the pen’s ink lying on the blue ring it follows.

steps.title: The chart is drawn on its marks, and the words last
steps.line: Objects, then words; no ink strays over 0.005 from its mark.
steps.caption: The planks, hanging tags and rope follow the fixed marks; the words fit the boxes those marks define. The drawing seed also places sea strokes and gulls, which can move without changing the chart’s geometry. This visual treatment follows the credited pele-art-diagrams examples. Which of these marks would a second drawing move?

steps.title: Traced on fixed marks, all 8 words stay in their boxes
steps.line: Top: the opening’s drawing. Bottom: the same chart traced on its marks.
steps.caption: Both drawings have imperfect strokes. In the upper one, every error rode along into the lines after it, displacing boxes from the words. Below, each stroke starts from its own fixed mark, so the 8 words fit their boxes. The difference comes from how this model constructs the route, not from making its pen perfectly steady.
